value.name: asks what the question is
value.description: A speaker asks what the question is, prompting Daniel to explain what he needs to know.

value.name: Daniel questions his mother's awareness
value.description: Daniel asks whether his mother knew he was only pretending to be a good son in her final years.
evidence: "Did she know," he said. "Did she know that I was — that I was the way I was. With her. In the last years. Did she know that I was performing being a good son rather than being one."

value.name: Daniel wonders about the codicil
value.description: Daniel asks whether his mother saw through him and changed the codicil because of it.
evidence: "Did she see through it. Did she — was the codicil — was it because she saw through it."

value.name: Daniel weighs two possible hurts
value.description: Daniel says he cannot decide whether it would be worse if his mother saw through him or if she did not and still left the house to Rosa and Lucia.
evidence: "I do not know which would be worse. I need someone who was there to tell me what she saw."

"I have been thinking about this since Wednesday and I cannot work out whether the worst thing is that she saw through it or the worst thing is that she did not see through it and made the codicil anyway because she had simply, on the merits and without reference to my failures, decided that you and Lucia deserved the house more than I did."

value.name: Rosa prepares to answer
value.description: Rosa pauses and breathes in, recognizing that she has long imagined how to answer Daniel's question.
evidence: "She had imagined this question. She had imagined it for years."

value.name: Rosa rehearses possible answers
value.description: Rosa mentally reviews multiple versions of her answer depending on what kind of man Daniel has become.
evidence: "She had imagined answering it in several different ways depending on the man Daniel had become by the time he asked it, and she had imagined that the worst version of the answer would be the version she gave to the worst version of him, and the best version of the answer would be the version she gave to the best version of him, and she had imagined, also, that the man asking the question might have become a different man by the asking of it, and that the answer might therefore have to be adjusted in the moment."

value.name: Rosa studies Daniel across the table
value.description: Rosa looks at Daniel and notices his unshaven appearance and unfinished coffee as she prepares to respond.
evidence: "She looked at him across the table. He had not shaved. He had ordered his coff"
